sections.title: Embedding
sections.blurb: A token is a row of feature words. cat is animal, furry, meow and four-legs.

sections.title: RMSNorm
sections.blurb: RMSNorm keeps the mix of words and sets their overall length to 1.

sections.title: SwiGLU
sections.blurb: SwiGLU mixes words inside the token. It never reads or writes the notebook.

sections.title: Block
sections.blurb: The token keeps its own words. The notebook's read is added on top, softly.

sections.title: Split into heads
sections.blurb: One projection makes query, key and value. Head 1 keeps animal and furry. Head 2 keeps meow and four-legs.

after.text: SCI-1 has the learned clock on, so this fixed-rope branch does not run. The turn is _rotate_learned.

sections.title: Learned clock
sections.blurb: Each head has a speed. The angle is the sum of speeds so far, times that pair's pace. Query and key turn together. Value does not.

sections.title: Retention
sections.blurb: Retention is how much of the previous page survives. It sits in (0, 1).

sections.title: Train: whole document
sections.blurb: A full document runs this call. The notebook update is the same one-token step, packed into a solve.

sections.title: Erase and write
sections.blurb: Erase and write are two strengths read from this token.

sections.title: Infer: one token
sections.blurb: Inference carries the notebook in, updates it with this one token, and carries it out. The page does not grow with context.

sections.title: Which path
sections.blurb: More than one token takes the chunked path. A single new token takes the step. Then a gate and the output projection.

sections.title: Shared read
sections.blurb: A block with no notebook asks the notebook below, in that writer's own clock.

sections.title: Tied scores
sections.blurb: Each vocab word is scored by a dot product of its embedding with the hidden words.

sections.title: Stack wiring
sections.blurb: EOS zeros retention so the old page stops at the document edge. The next reader receives the notebook the writer just exposed.

sections.title: Echo
sections.blurb: Echo files this token's embedding under the previous token's hidden words: the word that followed a state like that one.

sections.title: Head
sections.blurb: The tied head turns hidden words into vocab scores. Echo is added here and starts at zero.

sections.title: Loss
sections.blurb: Training scores the next word. At cat the asked word is sat. Inference stops at the scores.

sections.title: Same update, solved
sections.blurb: The chunked form is the same fade, erase and write, packed as one triangular solve per window.

sections.title: Fast path
sections.blurb: Training calls this. It is the same recurrence, solved in a batch. Autograd flows through the torch ops.

sections.title: Scan backward
sections.blurb: Hand-written backward of the additive scan under the delta solve. It is not a line-by-line dS loop.

lines.title: Look up the token's words
lines.train: Every token in the document is looked up. cat's row is animal, furry, meow, four-legs.
lines.infer: Only the newest token is looked up. The notebook from earlier tokens is already in hand.

lines.title: Length 1, mix unchanged
lines.train: The mix of words stays. Their overall length becomes 1, so a loud token and a quiet one are comparable.
lines.infer: Same norm on the single new token.

lines.title: Mix words inside the token
lines.train: Gate, up, product, down. Animal stays animal. Nothing is written to a notebook.
lines.infer: The same mix, on this token only.

lines.title: SwiGLU inside the block
lines.train: The block normalises the token, then mixes its words. The notebook is the next add.
lines.infer: Same mix for the token that just arrived.

lines.title: Keep the token, add the mix
lines.train: The original words stay. The SwiGLU mix is added on top.
lines.infer: The carried notebook is not in this add. It joins at the PAM line.

lines.title: No notebook here: read the one below
lines.train: This block has no page of its own. It asks the nearest notebook underneath.
lines.infer: The ask uses the notebook the writer carried to this token.

lines.title: Run the notebook
lines.train: The whole document goes through the chunked notebook.
lines.infer: One token goes through the step, with the notebook handed in.

lines.title: Add the read, softly
lines.train: The read is added with a small scale (it starts at 0.1) so the token's own words still carry the sentence.
lines.infer: Same add. The scale is a learned number, not a growing cache.

lines.title: Project the token
lines.train: One matrix makes query, key and value for every head.
lines.infer: The same matrix, on this token.

lines.title: Three views of the same token
lines.train: Head 1's cat is animal and furry. Head 2's cat is meow and four-legs. Value on head 1 has learned to carry sits.
lines.infer: Same split. Only this token is projected; the clock and the notebook arrive from before.

lines.title: Hand query and key to the clock
lines.train: Chrono is on, so this is the branch that runs. Value is not turned.
lines.infer: The clock is the number carried from the previous token, not the token's index.

lines.title: Fixed rope, not this run
lines.train: This turns pairs by position index. SCI-1 has the learned clock on, so this line does not run.
lines.infer: Decode would use the same fixed table. This model uses the carried clock instead.

lines.title: This token's speed
lines.train: A learned number per head, from the token's words. Slow keeps later keys close. Fast spins them apart.
lines.infer: The speed is computed from this token alone. The angle is the speed plus the clock handed in.

lines.title: Angle before this token
lines.train: The turn applied here is the sum of earlier speeds, not this token's own speed. The first token has not turned yet.
lines.infer: tau is the clock carried in. After the token, the clock handed on includes this speed.

lines.title: Each pair has its own pace
lines.train: animal–furry turns quickly. sits–soft barely moves. The pace is 10000^(−i/2), the same table as rope.
lines.infer: The carried clock is multiplied by that same pace.

lines.title: Turn the query
lines.train: The animal–furry pair is a pointer. The clock rotates it. A quarter turn would swap animal for furry.
lines.infer: Same turn. Query and key of this token share it, so this token still matches itself.

lines.title: Turn the key by the same angle
lines.train: Key and query share the angle, so a token still matches itself. A later token, turned further, matches it less.
lines.infer: The key that gets stored is this turned key. A later query has to turn by the same clock to find it.

lines.title: How much of the page survives
lines.train: exp(−softplus(·)) is between 0 and 1. EOS will multiply this by 0.
lines.infer: The carried page is faded by this number, then the token writes.

lines.title: Key length becomes 1
lines.train: The direction of the key is the address. Its length is set to 1 so a loud token and a quiet one write equally hard.
lines.infer: Same unit key on the single token.

lines.title: EOS drops the old page
lines.train: keep is 0 on the separator. Retention becomes 0, so the previous document does not cross the edge.
lines.infer: The next document starts from a blank carry. This line is what makes that true.

lines.title: Read the erase and write strengths
lines.train: Both gates are read from the token, once, and shared by the chunked path and the step.
lines.infer: Same two numbers on the token that just arrived.

lines.title: Write the whole document
lines.train: This is the call a training document actually makes. The grids are the same fade, erase and write as the one-token step.
lines.infer: Inference does not run this whole-document call. It repeats the one-token step and carries the notebook.

lines.title: Read, then scale
lines.train: The read is the notebook dotted with the query. The real model divides by √128. This picture divides by √4.
lines.infer: Same dot product. The notebook is the one just written.

lines.title: Erase strength
lines.train: sigmoid(· − 3), capped at 0.95. High erase clears the old value filed under this key.
lines.infer: Same gate on the new token.

lines.title: Write strength
lines.train: sigmoid of a projection of the token. High write plants this token's value on its key.
lines.infer: Same gate. EOS in this story writes almost nothing, so a zero retention leaves a blank page.

lines.title: Key length becomes 1
lines.train: The address is a direction. Training's chunked call normalises the same way.
lines.infer: The key carried into the update has length 1. The word mix is unchanged.

lines.title: What the page already says about this key
lines.train: S times the key is the value currently filed under this address.
lines.infer: The carried page is asked: what did you store under this key?

lines.title: Take the old value off this key
lines.train: Subtract erase × (page · key) × key. Other addresses stay. In train mode the grid below shows what the loss asks of this page.
lines.infer: Same subtract, on the carried page, before the fade and the write.

lines.title: Fade, then write the new value
lines.train: S = retain × erased + write × value × key. The loss pushes the cells that would make the next word more likely.
lines.infer: This is the whole memory update. The result is the notebook handed to the next token.

lines.title: Read: notebook dot query
lines.train: Each output word is a sum of (value × key) · query-key. The cells below are those products.
lines.infer: The query asks the page that was just written, including this token's own write.

lines.title: Divide by √d
lines.train: The real head uses √128. The picture uses √4, so four terms stay readable.
lines.infer: Same scale on the one-token read.

lines.title: Long document: chunked path
lines.train: Training feeds the whole document, so this branch runs and calls the batched delta.
lines.infer: A decode step has length 1, so this branch does not run.

lines.title: One token: the step
lines.train: Training does not use this branch for a full document. The math matches the chunked call.
lines.infer: This is the inference path. Notebook and clock come in, one token updates them, both go out.

lines.title: How much of the read to let out
lines.train: A per-head gate. It starts open (silu of the bias is 1) and can learn to shut a head.
lines.infer: The gate is a word on this token: open, or shut.

lines.title: Heads back into one list of words
lines.train: Head 1's four words and head 2's four words are concatenated and mixed back to the token width.
lines.infer: Same projection. The notebook itself stays behind; only this read comes out.

lines.title: Turn the reader's query into the writer's clock
lines.train: The reader has no clock of its own. It uses the cos and sin the writer stored.
lines.infer: At decode the writer exposes its current rotation with the notebook.

lines.title: Dot the shared notebook
lines.train: Same dot product as the writer's read. The page is the writer's page.
lines.infer: The carried notebook is dotted with this turned query.

lines.title: Reader's output gate
lines.train: The reader's out-projection starts at zero, so this add is off until it learns. The picture shows the read anyway.
lines.infer: Same gate. The notebook still belongs to the writer.

lines.title: Score every vocab word
lines.train: Hidden words dotted with cat, sat, mat, eos. The loss marks the next word. The residual still looks like the current word; the notebook's own vote is shown beside it.
lines.infer: The winning word is the guess. There is no target.

lines.title: Separator mask
lines.train: 1 on ordinary tokens, 0 on EOS. Multiplied into retention so the page cannot cross a document.
lines.infer: The carry after EOS is blank, so the next document does not see this one.

lines.title: Hand the reader the current notebook
lines.train: shared is whatever the last writer exposed. A block with its own notebook ignores it and writes a new one.
lines.infer: At decode, shared is the writer's state and rotation after this token.

lines.title: A writer exposes its page
lines.train: After a notebook block, the next readers see this page and this clock.
lines.infer: The exposed state is the carried notebook, not a growing cache.

lines.title: Key is the previous token
lines.train: The key at this token is the previous hidden state. The first token has no previous state, so its key is 0 and it writes nothing.
lines.infer: The previous hidden is part of the echo carry, next to the echo notebook.

lines.title: Value is this token's embedding
lines.train: The value is the embedding words of the token that is here now. At sat, those words get filed under cat.
lines.infer: Same binding, one token at a time.

lines.title: Normalise the embedding value
lines.train: The value's length is set by RMS, so the filed word is a direction.
lines.infer: Same norm on the new token's row.

lines.title: Unit key, from the previous hidden
lines.train: The address is the previous token's hidden words, length 1.
lines.infer: The address was carried as the previous hidden.

lines.title: EOS stops echo too
lines.train: Retention is 0 on the separator, and the key is zeroed, so nothing is filed and nothing crosses.
lines.infer: The echo carry after EOS is a blank page.

lines.title: Echo uses the same delta rule
lines.train: Fade, erase, write. The value is the embedding, the key is the previous hidden.
lines.infer: A one-token echo step does the same update just below, in the decode branch.

lines.title: File this word under the previous one
lines.train: At sat, sits is written under cat's animal and furry. That is the word that followed cat.
lines.infer: The echo notebook carried out holds that binding.

lines.title: Echo's read, starting from zero
lines.train: The out-projection starts at zero, so echo does not move the scores until it learns. The picture shows the page it is building.
lines.infer: The read is the embedding words recalled by a query that looks like the previous state.

lines.title: Run echo on the hidden words
lines.train: Echo sees the hidden state after the stack, and the token ids.
lines.infer: The echo notebook and the previous hidden are the extra carry.

lines.title: Add echo onto the scores
lines.train: Added after the tied projection. The add starts at zero because echo_out starts at zero.
lines.infer: Once it has learned, this is a recalled embedding added to the hidden words.

lines.title: Scores for the next word
lines.train: cat is scored against sat, the word that should follow. The mark is the target, not the winner.
lines.infer: The largest score is the guess. No loss, no target.

lines.title: Push toward the next word
lines.train: Cross-entropy on the next token. The push on the notebook is the grid of want-more and want-less.
lines.infer: Inference does not run the loss. The scores are the end of the step.

lines.title: The recurrence the solve implements
lines.train: Same formula as the one-token step. The solve is a fast way to run it on a window.
lines.infer: Decode does not use the solve. It runs the formula directly.

lines.title: One solve for the window
lines.train: The triangular solve builds the written values for every token in the window at once. The page you see is that result.
lines.infer: A single token has nothing to solve. The step writes one outer product.

lines.title: Batch the solve
lines.train: This is the speed rewrite of the same recurrence. Autograd goes through these torch ops.
lines.infer: Inference does not call this. Open the one-token step.

lines.title: Scan the solved values
lines.train: After the solve, one scan reads the notebook. Its backward is the kernel below.
lines.infer: The step reads with a plain dot product instead of this scan.

lines.title: Gradients of the scan
lines.train: The loss walks back through the scan. These tensors are the pushes on query, key, value and retention.
lines.infer: Inference does not run backward.

lines.title: Pushes on query, key and value
lines.train: dq, dk and dv are how the next-word loss wants those three vectors to change.
lines.infer: No loss, so these pushes are not computed.

lines.title: Push on retention
lines.train: How the loss wants the fade to change. EOS has retention 0, so the push stops at the document edge.
lines.infer: Not computed at decode.

lines.title: What the kernel hands back
lines.train: dq, dk, dv, d(retention), and the push into the carried notebook. The delta solve's own autograd sits on top of this.
lines.infer: This return does not run in inference.
